stories.head: Marketers deploying AI agents faster than they can measure them
stories.plain: Most marketing teams are rolling out AI agents without being able to link those agents' conversations to campaigns, conversions, or revenue. This measurement gap matters because buying and budgeting decisions depend on knowing what works — and right now, teams are flying blind on a fast-moving investment.

stories.head: Meet your new teammate: Building marketing workflows around AI agents
stories.plain: From the November MarTech Conference, this piece lays out how to design workflows that mix AI agent efficiency with human oversight and governance. It's practical guidance on where human judgment must stay in the loop — directly relevant to anyone deciding how to structure an AI-assisted marketing team.

stories.head: Scrunch launches Citation Optimization to help brands influence the sources behind AI recommendations
stories.plain: Sitecore's Scrunch tool now shows marketers which third-party publishers and reviewers shape what AI engines recommend — and helps them act on that intelligence. This is a concrete new product in the fast-growing Generative Engine Optimization category, changing how brands think about visibility in AI-generated answers.

stories.head: Iterable opens its platform to Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor with a hosted MCP server
stories.plain: Iterable now lets external AI models like Claude and ChatGPT connect directly to its customer engagement platform via a hosted MCP server, plus adds AI-assisted SDKs and an expanded integrations hub. This shifts how CEPs get bought and built — teams can wire their preferred AI into campaign execution without custom engineering.

stories.head: AppsFlyer expands Agentic AI and MCP tools with governed automation infrastructure
stories.plain: AppsFlyer's expanded Agent Hub lets marketing teams query and act on measurement data through automated agentic workflows, with explicit governance guardrails built into the architecture. It signals that measurement platforms are becoming agentic orchestration layers — and that governance is now a selling point, not an afterthought.

stories.head: Marketers deploying AI agents faster than they can measure them
stories.plain: Brands are rolling out AI agents across campaigns at speed, but most still cannot link those agent-driven conversations to actual conversions or revenue. This measurement gap is a serious governance and accountability problem: you can't manage what you can't measure, and untracked agents create budget and attribution blind spots that will compound fast.

stories.head: IAB unveils framework for measuring AI's part in conversions
stories.plain: The IAB has released a common attribution standard so brands and platforms can agree on how much credit AI-driven touchpoints deserve when a sale closes. This is a foundational governance move: without shared rules, every vendor will claim full credit and budgets will mis-allocate. Expect this to shape how MarTech contracts and reporting are written in 2027.

stories.head: Iterable opens its platform to Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor with a hosted MCP server
stories.plain: Iterable now exposes its customer engagement data to external AI models via a hosted Model Context Protocol server, letting tools like Claude or ChatGPT read and act on campaign data directly. This is a structural shift in how CEPs get built: instead of bespoke integrations, a standard protocol lets any capable AI agent plug in and run marketing workflows at scale.

stories.head: Scrunch launches Citation Optimization to help brands influence sources behind AI recommendations
stories.plain: Scrunch (a Sitecore company) now shows marketers which third-party publishers and reviewers shape AI-generated answers about their brand, then helps them target those sources to earn more citations. This is a concrete, buyable GEO product — the first wave of tools turning AI-answer visibility from a theory into a managed channel with measurable tactics.

stories.head: HubSpot brings back co-founder Brian Halligan as CEO to rebuild around AI
stories.plain: Yamini Rangan is out after five years; Halligan returns explicitly to reorganize HubSpot's product, go-to-market, and culture around AI. HubSpot is one of the largest SMB marketing platforms globally, so a founder-led AI pivot at this scale signals a coming wave of product and pricing changes that will affect how hundreds of thousands of businesses buy and use MarTech.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: The Agentic Flood: Deploying AI Agents Faster Than You Can Govern Them
body: Every major platform — Constant Contact, AppsFlyer, ActiveCampaign, Nectar, DomoAI — shipped an autonomous or semi-autonomous AI agent this month. The pace is striking: products that would have required months of integration work are launching in weeks, promising to handle campaign execution, creator activation, and CRM automation with minimal human input.

The governance gap is widening. MarTech's own reporting flags that marketers are deploying these agents before they have metrics to judge whether they are working. Without measurement frameworks, teams risk optimising for agent activity rather than business outcomes — a classic proxy-metric trap, now running at machine speed.
ev: MarTech · Automation is dead, long live automation

themes.head: MCP as Infrastructure: AI Becomes the Universal Integration Layer
body: Webflow, Iterable, and AppsFlyer all released Model Context Protocol connectors this month, allowing large language models like Claude and ChatGPT to query and act inside their platforms directly. MCP is quietly becoming what REST APIs were in the 2010s: the lingua franca that lets tools talk to each other — except now the caller is an AI agent, not a developer.

This changes the martech stack's architecture fundamentally. Point-to-point integrations are giving way to a hub model where a reasoning layer orchestrates multiple tools via a shared protocol. Teams that understand MCP now will have a structural advantage as AI-to-tool connections multiply; those that don't will find their stacks increasingly unmanageable.

themes.head: Measuring AI-Attributed Conversions Is Now a Board-Level Problem
body: The IAB released a formal framework for attributing conversions that touch AI-driven touchpoints, and MarTech published guidance on building cross-channel measurement for an AI-first media landscape. These are signals that the industry has accepted a hard truth: last-click and even multi-touch models break down when AI agents, chatbot referrals, and generative search are part of the funnel.

ChatGPT's paid traffic converting far worse than Google's crystallises the stakes — not all AI-driven traffic is equal, and without better attribution, budget will flow toward channels that look good in dashboards rather than channels that drive revenue. Marketers combining Marketing Mix Modelling with post-purchase surveys are emerging as the measurement vanguard.
ev: MarTech · ChatGPT traffic value vs Google

themes.head: The Expertise Erosion Risk Hidden Inside AI Productivity Gains
body: Two sharp opinion pieces this month — on the hidden cost of AI marketing and on what happens to enterprise SaaS when everyone can make software — converge on the same warning: AI productivity gains are real, but they can hollow out the institutional knowledge needed to course-correct when models go wrong. When AI writes the brief, executes the campaign, and reports the results, humans lose the feedback loops that build judgment.

This is not a hypothetical. Forrester's Joe Cicman frames it structurally: if everyone can ship software, the moat shifts from tooling to taste and domain expertise. For marketing teams, that means deliberately protecting spaces where humans still do hard strategic thinking — not as a romantic gesture, but as a competitive hedge against the moment AI outputs become undifferentiated.
ev: Agile Brand · Hidden cost of AI expertise
Agile Brand · Forrester on enterprise SaaS

themes.head: Brands Must Optimise for AI Recommendation Engines, Not Just Search Rankings
body: Scrunch's launch of Citation Optimisation and MarTech's piece on relevance having an expiration date both point to the same structural shift: the new discovery layer is an AI recommendation engine, not a search results page. When ChatGPT, Perplexity, or a shopping agent recommends a brand, it cites sources — and those citations are becoming the new first-page rankings that CMOs need to manage.

This rewrites content strategy from top-of-funnel SEO to something closer to PR-meets-data-engineering: ensuring authoritative sources cite your brand accurately and frequently enough that AI models surface you in generative answers. Optimove's piece on connecting with shoppers when the buyer is not human adds another layer — B2C brands now need to market to AI agents making autonomous purchasing decisions on behalf of human consumers.

month.takeaway: Every theme this month circles the same inflection point: AI is shifting from a tool marketers use to an actor that buys, recommends, and executes alongside them — and the strategies, metrics, and org structures built for the old model are expiring fast.
